pl-l4d21c7-d1e115.summary: Asks whether a confession avails in which the individual sins one committed are not expressed.

pl-l4d21c7-d1e118.summary: Answers that all mortal sins must be expressed at least once in confession, unless they have slipped from the mind. But since (sentence continues).
claims: Mortal sins must be named at least once, unless forgotten.

pl-l4d21c7-d1e121.summary: Completes: no one understands all his offenses, confess at least generally those you do not remember, and so you have hidden nothing. Venial sins, being innumerable, may be confessed generally, unless some are often repeated, though naming them is more perfect if possible. So a general confession is made daily in the Church for daily venial sins and for mortal sins of which we are unaware.
claims: Venial sins may be confessed generally.
The Church's daily confession covers venial and unknown sins.

pl-l4d21c7-d1e125.summary: Quotes Augustine: the penitent tells God the truth when he hides none of his crimes from him, not because God would not know, but because God wants the truth told to forgive; if some have slipped from his mind, he confesses the truth by saying generally: God who knows the secrets of hearts, my works and offenses are not hidden from you; forgive them. This is the truth of the one confessing that God loves.
claims: Confessing generally what one has forgotten is truthful confession.

pl-l4d21c7-d1e140.summary: Draws out that general confession deletes even mortal sins of which one is unaware.
claims: General confession deletes unknown mortal sins.

pl-l4d21c7.summary: Asks whether a confession that does not name each sin avails. All mortal sins must be named at least once, unless forgotten; those forgotten should be confessed generally, so nothing is concealed. Venial sins, being innumerable, may be confessed generally, unless often repeated, though naming them is more perfect; hence the Church's daily general confession for venial sins and unknown mortal ones. Augustine: the penitent tells God the truth when he hides nothing, and if some are forgotten, he tells the truth by confessing generally. So general confession deletes even unknown mortal sins.
claims: All mortal sins must be confessed specifically at least once, unless forgotten.
Forgotten sins are covered by general confession.
Venial sins may be confessed generally.
General confession deletes unknown mortal sins.
